game_crew_assignment.description: One regular-season game's officiating crew, resolved to individual official_ids rather than to the referee's name. crew_id is derived as <season>-ref<referee official_id>, because no upstream publishes a crew key and NFL crews are identified publicly by their white hat. assignment_announced_at and is_provisional are null BY NECESSITY, not by omission: the only free upstream (nflverse officials.csv) is a post-game record of who worked a game, and carries no publication instant and no provisional flag. null_field_reason states that on every row.

game_id.description: The modern nflverse id (2025_01_DAL_PHI), joined from officials.csv's legacy gamekey through games.csv's published old_game_id column.

crew_members.description: The on-field crew. Alternates and the replay official are excluded: they appear irregularly and do not throw flags, so counting them would read as churn on exactly the games where one happened to be recorded.

assignment_announced_at.description: NULL BY NECESSITY. When the crew was published. No free upstream carries it; a paid or scraped forward-looking assignment feed (Football Zebras publishes crews midweek) would have to supply it.

is_provisional.description: NULL BY NECESSITY. Whether the assignment is subject to change. Same upstream gap as assignment_announced_at -- a post-game record cannot be provisional.

crew_continuity_pct.description: Share of this assignment's crew_members also on this crew_id across the sampled window, averaged over the members. Below 0.6 with the crew's rates being served raises the spec's separate alarm.

games_sampled.description: Size of this crew's rate window. 0 when play-by-play was unavailable, which is the degraded pass.

crew_tendency_rates.description: One crew's rate profile over its sampled window. Every rate is an object rather than a bare float -- see $defs/rate. Rates are regressed toward the league mean by a random-effects weight rather than published as raw window means, and a rate whose split-half correlation is not distinguishable from zero is REFUSED (value null) unless it was shrunk, which is the spec's stated rule implemented rather than noted.

rate.description: One crew rate, with everything a consumer needs to judge it. The spec's field table lists is_shrunk (bool) and rate_stderr (float) as scalar fields of the signal; they cannot be, because there are eight rates with independent sample variances and independent stability verdicts and one bool cannot describe eight of them. So each spec-named rate field carries this object instead. `value` is null when the rate was REFUSED -- its split-half correlation was indistinguishable from zero and the estimate was not shrunk -- while `raw` survives the refusal, because a consumer doing its own statistics is entitled to the observation. $defs lives INSIDE this signal type rather than at the document root because both conformance gates extract signal_types[<name>] and validate it standalone, which leaves a root-level $ref pointing at nothing.

value.description: The served rate: the shrunk estimate when is_shrunk, the raw window mean otherwise, and null when served is false.

raw.description: The unadjusted mean over games_sampled. Published even when the rate is refused.

stderr.description: The spec's rate_stderr: sqrt(pooled within-crew variance / games_sampled). The standard error of the raw mean at this sample size.

is_shrunk.description: The spec's is_shrunk: whether the published value was regressed toward the league mean by a materially-less-than-one weight.

shrinkage_factor.description: tau2 / (tau2 + sigma2/n). 0 means no evidence this crew differs from the league at all; 1 means the crew's own mean survives untouched.

split_half_r.description: Pearson correlation between crews' odd-week and even-week means for this rate, across every sampled crew. null when the sample cannot answer the question (fewer than two crews, or no variance).

split_half_ci_low.description: Lower bound of the Fisher-z 95% interval on split_half_r. Greater than zero is what 'distinguishable from zero' means. null below four crews, where the interval is undefined.

games_sampled.description: The spec's games_sampled: games behind every rate below. Uniform across rates because a game only enters the window when play-by-play carries it with at least one offensive snap.
